Looking at the choices offered (Ainok Bond-Kin, Forest, Abzan Falconer), playing Forest first is strictly better sequencing since it gives access to 4 mana total (Plains, Forest, Sol Ring = {W}{G}{C}{C}), which doesn't change what can be cast this turn but is good practice. More importantly, with 4 mana after playing Forest, they could cast Ainok Bond-Kin ({1}{W}) and still have {G}{C} left over - though nothing else costs that. Alternatively, Abzan Falconer at {2}{W} uses 3 of 4 mana. The Falconer is arguably the better card (2/3 vs 2/1, flying vs first strike), so the creature choice is reasonable. But they should have played Forest first before casting the spell - casting spells before playing lands is a sequencing error.

Given that Johnny's deck contains Beast creatures (Ravenous Baloth, Marath, and the Beast token from One Dozen Eyes), getting Contested Cliffs into play early provides a repeatable removal engine. Playing Forest here is slightly worse since Johnny already has a Selesnya Guildgate for green mana and Sol Ring for colorless. The Contested Cliffs only produces colorless like Sol Ring already does, but its fight ability is a unique and powerful effect worth establishing early. However, Johnny does need colored mana for expensive spells like Warstorm Surge (5R) and One Dozen Eyes (5G), so a basic Forest has some merit for mana development.

annotations.description: Attacking with a 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn token deals 0 damage and accomplishes nothing. The token is more valuable as a mana source (sacrifice for {C}) or as a chump blocker. Sending it into combat risks losing it to any blocker while dealing no damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with the 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn token against GLM47 Gramps.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the Eldrazi Spawn token back as a potential mana source or chump blocker. It deals 0 damage on attack, so there's no upside to attacking with it unless you specifically want it to die (which doesn't appear to be the case here).

annotations.description: Playing Boros Garrison before casting a creature is slightly suboptimal but not terrible. Boros Garrison enters tapped and requires bouncing a land, which means the player loses mana availability this turn. With 4 mana available (Selesnya Guildgate, Sol Ring, Forest, Contested Cliffs), they could cast Drumhunter (3G) or Ravenous Baloth (2GG) first, then play Boros Garrison next turn. By playing Garrison now, they bounce a land and end up with all tapped lands, unable to cast anything meaningful this turn. However, Garrison does fix red mana for future turns and the player may be planning ahead. The Howling Mine trigger means they'll draw extra cards, so developing mana isn't unreasonable.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Boros Garrison, which enters tapped and bounces a land, leaving limited mana available this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Drumhunter (3G) using Forest + Sol Ring + Selesnya Guildgate + Contested Cliffs to develop the board and set up card draw, then play Boros Garrison next turn when the tempo loss of a tapped land matters less.

annotations.description: Bouncing Boros Garrison to hand means it must be replayed next turn and will enter tapped again, costing a full turn of mana development. Boros Garrison produces 2 mana (RW) when untapped. By returning it, Johnny loses access to that mana this turn cycle and next turn must replay it tapped again, effectively wasting two land drops on the same land. Returning Selesnya Guildgate (which only produces G or W, a subset of what Boros Garrison provides) or Contested Cliffs (which requires RG to activate and has limited utility early) would have been better. Returning a basic Forest would keep the bounce land in play producing 2 mana, though Forest is untapped. The best return is likely Selesnya Guildgate since Boros Garrison already produces both colors Guildgate would, and Guildgate entered tapped previously anyway.
annotations.actionTaken: Returned Boros Garrison (the land just played) to hand, creating an infinite bounce loop where the same land must be replayed tapped next turn.
annotations.betterLine: Return Selesnya Guildgate to hand. Boros Garrison already covers G and W mana production, and Guildgate is strictly worse. This keeps Boros Garrison on the battlefield to untap next turn and produce RW, while Guildgate can be replayed later if needed.

annotations.description: Putting the +1/+1 counter on Leinore instead of Ainok Bond-Kin misses out on activating Ainok Bond-Kin's first strike granting ability. Both targets enable coven (three distinct powers), but Ainok Bond-Kin with a counter would grant first strike to all creatures with +1/+1 counters, which is meaningful with Abzan Falconer also on board (future counters grant both flying and first strike).
annotations.actionTaken: Put the +1/+1 counter on Leinore, Autumn Sovereign
annotations.betterLine: Put the +1/+1 counter on Ainok Bond-Kin to activate its first strike granting ability while still enabling coven for the card draw

annotations.description: Putting the +1/+1 counter on Leinore (making her 1/5) misses the synergy of putting it on Ainok Bond-Kin, which would activate both Bond-Kin's first strike aura and Abzan Falconer's flying aura for Bond-Kin, creating a 3/2 flying first striker.
annotations.actionTaken: Put the +1/+1 counter from Leinore's coven trigger on Leinore herself, making her a 1/5.
annotations.betterLine: Put the +1/+1 counter on Ainok Bond-Kin to activate its first strike granting ability and gain flying from Abzan Falconer, creating a much more impactful board presence.

annotations.description: Attacking with the Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1) deals 0 damage and risks losing it if blocked, though GLM47 Gramps has Katsumasa (3/3 flying) which can't block a ground creature, and Silver Myr is tapped. The token has value as a sacrifice for {C} mana, which could be relevant for future plays. However, the attack deals 0 damage anyway since it's a 0/1, so it accomplishes nothing even if unblocked. The token's sacrifice ability for colorless mana could be more useful kept in reserve.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with the 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn Token, which deals 0 damage even if unblocked.
annotations.betterLine: Don't attack with the Eldrazi Spawn Token. It deals 0 damage and its sacrifice-for-mana ability has more value than a 0-damage attack. Keep it back as a potential blocker or mana source.

annotations.description: Katsumasa's upkeep trigger allows putting +1/+1 counters on up to three noncreature artifacts for free. GLM47 controls Sol Ring which is a noncreature artifact. Putting counters on it has no downside and makes it stronger when later animated by Katsumasa's activated ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to put +1/+1 counters on any noncreature artifacts (selected 0 targets).
annotations.betterLine: Should have targeted at least their own Sol Ring to accumulate +1/+1 counters for future animation with Katsumasa's ability.

annotations.description: GLM47 is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Surgehacker Mech, a powerful 5/5 menace Vehicle that deals damage on entry based on Vehicles controlled — which synergizes perfectly with Katsumasa, the Animator (who can animate artifacts and put +1/+1 counters on them). Katsumasa is already on the battlefield, making Surgehacker Mech a high-value card. Meanwhile, GLM47 has 3 Plains and 2 Islands in hand — they only need 1-2 more lands and could safely discard excess basic lands instead.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Surgehacker Mech as one of the two cards to discard to hand size.
annotations.betterLine: Discard a Plains (having 3 Plains in hand is excessive when only needing a couple more land drops) instead of the Surgehacker Mech, which has strong synergy with Katsumasa and represents a significant threat.

annotations.description: Boros Garrison enters tapped and requires bouncing a land. By bouncing itself, the player essentially wasted their entire land drop for the turn — they end up with the same number of lands in play as before (the Garrison replaces itself but is tapped), and they have to replay it next turn, losing another land drop to the bounce. This creates a two-turn tempo loss for no gain.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Boros Garrison back to hand when it entered the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Selesnya Guildgate (which only produces GW, colors already covered by Forest and the Garrison itself producing RW). This keeps 4 lands on the battlefield including the new Garrison, and replaying Selesnya Guildgate next turn is a clean land drop with no bounce cost. Alternatively, bouncing Contested Cliffs (which requires RG to activate and is situational) would also be better than bouncing the Garrison itself.

annotations.description: Playing Forest instead of Terramorphic Expanse is slightly suboptimal. Terramorphic Expanse should be played first because it enters untapped and can be cracked immediately (or later) to fetch any basic land needed, providing flexibility. Playing a basic Forest locks in the land choice now, whereas Terramorphic Expanse keeps options open and also thins the deck. Additionally, the player has Kynaios and Tiro of Meletis as their commander (RGWU), and Terramorphic Expanse could fetch whatever color is most needed at the time it's cracked. Playing the Forest from hand means the Terramorphic Expanse will be played on a later turn, delaying its utility by a turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest as their land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Terramorphic Expanse instead, keeping the Forest in hand for future flexibility or to put onto the battlefield via Kynaios and Tiro's end step trigger. Terramorphic Expanse could then be cracked to fetch whatever basic is most needed.

annotations.description: Akroan Horse is a 4-mana card that gives an opponent a 0/4 defender while giving you 1/1 tokens each upkeep - it's not great but it's not the worst discard. However, discarding Mountain seems strictly better here. Valley already has an Island and Forest on the battlefield plus Myriad Landscape, and has a Plains and Terramorphic Expanse in hand. The Mountain is the least useful card since Valley's colored mana needs (for cards like Gwafa Hazid which needs W/U, Windborn Muse which needs W, Humble Defector which needs R) can mostly be met by existing lands and the Terramorphic Expanse. Meanwhile, Akroan Horse at least has some utility as a token generator in multiplayer, and with Howling Mine drawing extra cards, Valley may want to deploy it eventually.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Akroan Horse
annotations.betterLine: Discard Mountain instead - it's the most redundant card given existing mana sources and cards in hand. Terramorphic Expanse can fetch a Mountain later if needed.

annotations.description: Attacking with all creatures (including Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin) is questionable. These are key outlast creatures that form the backbone of Coach's +1/+1 counter strategy. Without any counters on them yet, they're just small bodies (2/3 and 2/1) that could easily be blocked and killed. The Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1) also can't deal damage. Attacking into GLM47 Gramps who has Katsumasa (3/3 flyer) and Silver Myr available as blockers risks losing important synergy pieces for minimal damage. The Ainok Bond-Kin at 2/1 is particularly vulnerable. Coach should be developing their board and using outlast to build up counters rather than making ineffective attacks.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose 'All attack' sending Abzan Falconer (2/3), Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1), and Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1) into combat.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with no creatures or at most just the Eldrazi Spawn Token (which you might want to sacrifice for mana anyway). Focus on building the board - play Forest from hand, then use remaining mana to start outlasting Abzan Falconer or Ainok Bond-Kin in future turns, or play Bastion Protector to protect the commander when it comes down.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is discarding to hand size and chose to discard Exotic Orchard and an Island. Exotic Orchard is a versatile mana-fixing land that can produce any color an opponent's land could produce, which is especially valuable in a multiplayer game where opponents have diverse land bases. With only 4 lands in play (Island, Sol Ring, Silver Myr, Port Town) and Hanna, Ship's Navigator in hand (which costs 1WU), color fixing is important. Exotic Orchard would help cast multicolored spells and provide flexibility. Discarding two basic Islands instead would preserve the more valuable land while still reducing hand size.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Exotic Orchard and Island
annotations.betterLine: Discard two basic Plains or two basic Islands instead, keeping Exotic Orchard for its superior mana fixing in a multiplayer game where opponents control Forests, Mountains, and other diverse lands

annotations.description: Johnny is forced to discard 2 cards (likely down to hand size of 7). They chose to discard Mountain and Khalni Garden. However, Khalni Garden is a land that creates a 0/1 Plant token when it enters - it has real utility beyond just being a land. Meanwhile, Boros Guildgate is a strictly worse land option (enters tapped, only produces R or W which Boros Garrison already covers better). Discarding Boros Guildgate instead of Khalni Garden would have preserved a land that provides both mana fixing AND a free creature token, which synergizes with Warstorm Surge and Rampaging Baloths (landfall triggers). The Mountain discard is reasonable since they already have color sources, but Khalni Garden over Boros Guildgate is a value loss.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Mountain and Khalni Garden
annotations.betterLine: Discard Mountain and Boros Guildgate instead, keeping Khalni Garden for its enters-the-battlefield Plant token which synergizes with Rampaging Baloths landfall and future Warstorm Surge

annotations.description: Playing Gruul Turf enters tapped and bounces a land, leaving only Island + Forest (2 mana) available this turn. Playing Plains instead would give 3 untapped mana (Island + Forest + Plains), enabling an immediate cast of Gwafa Hazid, Profiteer (1WU) - a strong tempo play that could start neutralizing threats. The Gruul Turf can be played next turn after establishing board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Gruul Turf, which enters tapped and bounces a land, wasting the turn's mana development.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains to have Island + Forest + Plains untapped, then cast Gwafa Hazid, Profiteer (1WU) this turn. Save Gruul Turf for a later turn when the tempo loss matters less.

annotations.description: Bouncing Gruul Turf back to hand instead of a basic land means KimiK2 Valley loses a net land on the battlefield. Gruul Turf taps for RG (two mana), so bouncing it means replaying it next turn (entering tapped again) and losing tempo. By contrast, bouncing a basic land like Island or Forest would leave Gruul Turf on the battlefield producing RG, while the basic land could simply be replayed next turn untapped. The player ends up in a loop of replaying Gruul Turf repeatedly without net mana advancement. With a hand containing multiple lands to play (Plains, Terramorphic Expanse, Mountain) and expensive spells to cast (Windborn Muse at 4, Rubblehulk at 6, Reverse the Sands at 8), falling behind on mana development is costly.
annotations.actionTaken: Bounced Gruul Turf back to hand when it entered the battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Island (or Forest) to hand. This leaves Gruul Turf on the battlefield producing RG, and the basic land can be replayed untapped on a future turn, resulting in net mana gain rather than spinning wheels.

annotations.description: Discarded Rubblehulk instead of Reverse the Sands. Rubblehulk has a flexible Bloodrush ability ({1}{R}{G} to give an attacking creature +X/+X where X = lands controlled), making it useful even without casting it for 6 mana. Reverse the Sands costs 8 mana and is highly situational - currently all players are at 40 life except one at 21.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Rubblehulk as one of the two cards to discard to hand size
annotations.betterLine: Discard Reverse the Sands instead of Rubblehulk, keeping the more flexible and lower-cost bloodrush option available

annotations.description: With only 4 lands in play and needing to develop mana, discarding a basic Mountain (a land drop) over Reverse the Sands (an 8-mana situational spell they won't cast for many turns while at 40 life) is debatable. Extra land drops are valuable when behind on mana development.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Mountain as the second card (alongside Rubblehulk)
annotations.betterLine: Discard Reverse the Sands instead of Mountain, keeping the basic land to ensure hitting land drops with only 4 lands in play. Reverse the Sands is too expensive and too situational at 40 life to prioritize over mana development.

annotations.description: Shamanic Revelation draws cards equal to the number of creatures you control. Gem3F Coach controls only 3 creatures (Abzan Falconer, Ainok Bond-Kin, Eldrazi Spawn Token), so this draws only 3 cards for 5 mana with no Ferocious triggers (no creature has power 4+). More importantly, casting this 5-mana sorcery before playing the Forest from hand means less mana available this turn and potentially next turn. Additionally, casting Bastion Protector (3 mana) or Eternal Witness (3 mana, returning Growth Spasm for ramp) would develop the board more efficiently. Playing the Forest first, then casting Talisman of Unity (2 mana) would set up better future turns. The Shamanic Revelation for 3 cards isn't terrible, but the sequencing is wrong — the Forest should be played first, and there may be better uses of 5 mana when you only draw 3 cards and have no board development.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shamanic Revelation with only 3 creatures on board (drawing 3 cards) before playing a land from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest from hand first, then either cast Eternal Witness to recur Growth Spasm for future ramp, or cast Bastion Protector to develop the board. Save Shamanic Revelation for when you have more creatures for better value.

annotations.description: Cast Bastion Protector without a commander on the battlefield, making it just a vanilla 3/3. Meanwhile, the hand is loaded with expensive cards (Sigarda 5 mana, Cleansing Nova 5, Dearly Departed 6, Somberwald Beastmaster 7) that desperately need mana acceleration.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bastion Protector as a vanilla 3/3 with no commander to buff.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Heronblade Elite, which provides mana ramp that scales with subsequent Human entries. The hand is full of expensive Humans, and Heronblade Elite would accelerate deploying them while growing from each Human played.

annotations.description: GLM47 declined to interact with a 10/10 Herald of War and a 4/3 Ainok Bond-Kin attacking them for 14 damage total, dropping from 21 to 7 life. Herald of War is an escalating threat that grows every attack and was already enormous. At 7 life, GLM47 is in critical danger of dying to almost any subsequent attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority and took 14 damage from Herald of War (10/10) and Ainok Bond-Kin (4/3), going from 21 to 7 life.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Reality Shift targeting Herald of War to exile it, reducing incoming damage from 14 to 4 and removing the most dangerous threat on the board. This would leave GLM47 at 17 life instead of 7, a much safer position. Herald of War only grows larger each turn and needed to be answered.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life and chose not to block what appears to be an incoming attack (likely Abzan Falconer, a 2/3). Taking 2 damage at 2 life is lethal.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to assign any blockers despite being at 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Block with Katsumasa, the Animator (3/3) which would kill the Abzan Falconer (2/3) while Katsumasa survives, or at minimum chump block with Silver Myr to stay alive.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life and chose to put all three +1/+1 counters on Sol Ring, which is their own artifact. Katsumasa's upkeep trigger lets you put counters on up to three target noncreature artifacts - these could be different artifacts. The player could have targeted opponent artifacts like Howling Mine (which is actively hurting them by giving opponents extra cards while they're at 2 life) or other opponent artifacts. More importantly, they're putting all 3 counters on Sol Ring when they could spread them across different artifacts. However, the biggest issue is that Sol Ring is already their own artifact and they only seem to have Sol Ring and Silver Myr as artifacts (Silver Myr is a creature so it doesn't qualify as noncreature). They chose Sol Ring three times, putting 3 counters on it. But Katsumasa can animate noncreature artifacts into creatures - so buffing Sol Ring to later animate it as a bigger creature is a reasonable plan. Still, at 2 life, the Howling Mine giving all opponents extra draws is extremely dangerous. They should have targeted the opponent's Howling Mine with at least one counter to set up animating it or simply to have the option. Actually, looking more carefully - the choices offered were 'Abzan Falconer, Talisman of Unity, Sol Ring' which are the noncreature artifacts available. Abzan Falconer is a creature belonging to Gem3F Coach, Talisman of Unity isn't on anyone's board that I can see. Wait - the choices presented seem limited. The selected 2 of 3 message and the fact they chose Sol Ring suggests they already selected some targets. The final result shows all counters on Sol Ring. Given they're at 2 life, putting counters on Sol Ring to animate it as a blocker is reasonable, but putting all 3 on the same artifact rather than spreading them is suboptimal if other valid targets existed.
annotations.actionTaken: Put all +1/+1 counters on Sol Ring three times from Katsumasa's upkeep trigger
annotations.betterLine: Spread counters across different noncreature artifacts if possible, or target opponent artifacts like Howling Mine to set up animating/controlling the board better at 2 life

annotations.description: Discarding Command Tower is a significant mistake. Command Tower is one of the best lands in Commander, entering untapped and producing any color in your commander's color identity (RGW for Marath). Johnny needs to discard 2 cards from a hand of 9, and has Boros Guildgate (enters tapped, produces only R or W) and Boros Garrison (enters tapped, bounces a land) as clearly inferior land options. War Cadence is also a low-impact card in this board state. Discarding Command Tower over these weaker options loses significant mana fixing and tempo in future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Command Tower, one of the best fixing lands available.
annotations.betterLine: Discard Boros Guildgate and War Cadence (or Boros Garrison). Command Tower enters untapped and produces any color - it's strictly better than the tapped lands and the low-impact enchantment.

annotations.description: Playing Plains instead of Terramorphic Expanse is slightly suboptimal. Terramorphic Expanse can be cracked to fetch any basic land (including a Plains if needed), providing more flexibility for future turns and thinning the deck. Additionally, with Gruul Turf available, playing Terramorphic Expanse now (crack it for a basic) and then playing Gruul Turf next turn to bounce and replay a land would maximize mana development. The Plains is a fine play but Terramorphic Expanse provides strictly more flexibility since it can find any basic.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains as their land for the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Terramorphic Expanse, then sacrifice it to search for whatever basic land is most needed (likely a Plains anyway, but keeping the option open for Mountain or other basics). This also enables better synergy with Gruul Turf on a future turn.

annotations.description: Activating Myriad Landscape costs 2 mana and sacrifices the land, leaving KimiK2 Valley with only 4 lands (Island, Forest, Plains, and the two fetched basics) after resolution. With 5 mana available (Island, Myriad Landscape, Forest, Plains + the 2 from sacrificing), they could have cast Gwafa Hazid (1WU) or Windborn Muse (3W) this turn instead. More importantly, GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life with Katsumasa as a potential threat, and Gwafa Hazid could lock down Katsumasa or other threats. Myriad Landscape activation is fine long-term ramp, but sequencing matters - they should play the Gruul Turf or Terramorphic Expanse from hand first as their land drop, then decide whether to activate Myriad Landscape or cast a spell. Activating Myriad Landscape before making a land drop wastes the opportunity to play a land this turn alongside the activation.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Myriad Landscape as the first action in precombat main phase.
annotations.betterLine: Play Terramorphic Expanse (or Gruul Turf) as the land drop first, then decide between activating Myriad Landscape or casting Windborn Muse/Gwafa Hazid. Playing a land before sacrificing Myriad Landscape ensures no missed land drop.

annotations.description: With GLM47 Gramps at only 2 life, Windborn Muse would have been a strong defensive play - its flying body and attack tax ({2} per attacking creature) provides significant protection. Gwafa Hazid requires additional mana investment ({W}{U} + tap) to neutralize one creature at a time, and the controller draws a card as compensation. However, Gwafa does cost 1 less mana (3 vs 4), so casting him now when mana is tight is reasonable. The main concern is that Windborn Muse's passive protection is generally more impactful in a 4-player game where multiple opponents might attack, whereas Gwafa's activated ability is slow and card-disadvantageous.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Gwafa Hazid, Profiteer for {1}{W}{U}
annotations.betterLine: Cast Windborn Muse for {3}{W} - provides immediate flying blocker and passive attack deterrent without giving opponents cards. With only 5 lands and needing to develop further, the Muse's no-activation-cost protection is more efficient.

annotations.description: Casting Sigarda, Heron's Grace (5 mana) before playing a Forest from hand. Gem3F Coach has two Forests in hand and should play a land first to have more mana available for future turns or to potentially cast additional spells. Additionally, casting Heronblade Elite first (3 mana) would allow it to get a +1/+1 counter when Sigarda enters (since Sigarda is a Human triggering Heronblade Elite, though Sigarda is an Angel not a Human - wait, Heronblade Elite triggers on 'another Human enters'). Actually, Sigarda is an Angel, not a Human, so Heronblade Elite wouldn't trigger. However, the sequencing concern about playing a land before casting spells remains valid. Also, with Dearly Departed in the graveyard, Human creatures enter with an additional +1/+1 counter - but Sigarda is an Angel, not Human. Heronblade Elite IS a Human though, and would enter with an extra counter from Dearly Departed, making it a 2/2 with vigilance and mana production equal to its power. Casting Heronblade Elite first (3 mana), it enters as a 2/2 due to Dearly Departed, then with remaining mana after playing a land (would have 7 mana total with land drop), could still cast Sigarda (5 mana) - but that's 8 mana total needed. With current lands (4 lands + Sol Ring + Eldrazi Spawn = 7 mana), playing a Forest would give 8 mana. So the better line would be: Play Forest, cast Heronblade Elite (3 mana, enters as 2/2 from Dearly Departed), then cast Sigarda (5 mana, Heronblade Elite triggers getting another counter becoming 3/3). This generates significantly more value.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sigarda, Heron's Grace without playing a land first and before casting Heronblade Elite
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first, then cast Heronblade Elite (enters as 2/2 from Dearly Departed in graveyard), then cast Sigarda, Heron's Grace (triggers Heronblade Elite to become 3/3). This maximizes value from Dearly Departed and Heronblade Elite's trigger, while ensuring the land drop isn't missed.

annotations.description: Herald of War already has flying and each +1/+1 counter on it reduces the cost of Human and Angel spells by {1}. With a hand full of Humans (Eternal Witness, Heron's Grace Champion, Heronblade Elite, Yavimaya Elder), putting 2 counters on Herald would save {2} on each Human cast going forward - massive mana advantage. Sigarda already has flying naturally, so the counters give her less incremental value.
annotations.actionTaken: Put two +1/+1 counters on Sigarda, Heron's Grace (already has flying)
annotations.betterLine: Put two +1/+1 counters on Herald of War to get {2} cost reduction on the multiple Human spells in hand, while also making it a 5/5 flyer for attacking Gramps at 2 life

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F Coach has Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) that can attack. Gramps only has Katsumasa (3/3 flying) and Silver Myr (1/1) as potential blockers. Attacking with both creatures forces Gramps to block both or die - they'd need to use both blockers to survive. Even attacking with just one 2-power creature forces Gramps to chump block or die.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures, leaving an opponent at 2 life uncontested.
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Gramps with both Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin. Gramps must block both or die. This either eliminates a player or forces them to trade away their creatures.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life with only Katsumasa (3/3 flying) and Silver Myr (1/1) as blockers. Attacking with Herald of War (flying), Bastion Protector, and Ainok Bond-Kin at Gramps forces lethal - Katsumasa can block Herald (trade), Silver Myr can block one ground creature, but the other ground creature deals 2+ damage for the kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack for lethal against the 2-life opponent
annotations.betterLine: Attack Gramps with Herald of War, Bastion Protector, and Ainok Bond-Kin. With only two blockers available, at least one 2+ power creature gets through for lethal damage against 2 life.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life with only 2 potential blockers (Katsumasa the Animator 3/3 flying and Silver Myr 1/1). Attacking with 3+ creatures guarantees lethal since at least one attacker gets through unblocked for 2+ damage. Herald of War (flying), Ainok Bond-Kin, and Bastion Protector attacking would force Gramps to leave at least one unblocked.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack all or enough creatures at Gramps to guarantee lethal
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Herald of War, Ainok Bond-Kin, and Bastion Protector (or all creatures) directed at GLM47 Gramps to guarantee lethal damage through only 2 available blockers

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F Coach has Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) on the battlefield, plus an Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1). Attacking GLM47 Gramps with just one creature is correct in direction, but we need to check if lethal is achievable. Abzan Falconer is 2/3 and Ainok Bond-Kin is 2/1 — either one can deal 2 damage, which is exactly lethal against 2 life. Gramps has Katsumasa (3/3 flyer) and Silver Myr (1/1) as potential blockers. Since the attackers don't have flying or evasion (no +1/+1 counters on them yet), Katsumasa can block. However, the decision here is just choosing WHO to attack — and choosing Gramps at 2 life is clearly correct since that's the lethal target. The actual attack declaration (which creatures) comes next. This decision is correct.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to attack GLM47 Gramps who is at 2 life
annotations.betterLine: This is the correct choice — attacking the player at 2 life for the kill

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F Coach has Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) on the battlefield, plus an Eldrazi Spawn token. Attacking GLM47 Gramps with even just the Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) and Abzan Falconer (2/3) would deal lethal damage since Gramps only has Katsumasa (3/3) and Silver Myr (1/1) as potential blockers - but even if one is blocked, the other gets through for at least 2 damage which is exactly lethal. Instead, Coach chose to attack KimiK2 Valley, completely missing the lethal attack on a player at 2 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to attack KimiK2 Valley (40 life)
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Gramps (2 life) with multiple creatures to guarantee lethal damage. Even with Katsumasa and Silver Myr as blockers, attacking with all three creatures (Abzan Falconer, Ainok Bond-Kin, Eldrazi Spawn) guarantees at least 2 damage gets through for the kill.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F Coach has Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) on the battlefield, both untapped and able to attack. Attacking GLM47 Gramps with either creature would deal lethal damage (2 >= 2 life). GLM47 Gramps has Katsumasa, the Animator (3/3 flying) and Silver Myr (1/1) as potential blockers, but Abzan Falconer has 2 power and Ainok Bond-Kin has 2 power - sending both ensures lethal even if one is blocked. Instead, Coach chose to attack KimiK2 Valley at 40 life, completely missing the lethal opportunity to eliminate a player.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked KimiK2 Valley (40 life) instead of GLM47 Gramps (2 life).
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Gramps with Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin. Even if Katsumasa blocks one (3/3 vs 2/3 or 2/1), the other gets through for 2 damage, which is exactly lethal. Alternatively, even a single unblocked attacker deals lethal. Eliminating a player is a massive strategic advantage.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F Coach has Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) on the battlefield, along with an Eldrazi Spawn token. Attacking GLM47 Gramps with either the Falconer or the Bond-Kin (or both) would deal lethal damage (2 >= 2 life). Gramps has Katsumasa the Animator (3/3) and Silver Myr (1/1) as potential blockers, but even if one creature is blocked, the other would get through for lethal. Instead, Coach chose to attack KimiK2 Valley at 40 life, which accomplishes almost nothing compared to eliminating a player.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked KimiK2 Valley (40 life) instead of GLM47 Gramps (2 life).
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Gramps with Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin. Gramps has only Katsumasa (3/3) and Silver Myr (1/1) as potential blockers — blocking one attacker still lets the other through for 2 damage, which is lethal against 2 life. This eliminates a player from the game.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F Coach has Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) that could attack. Gramps only has Katsumasa (3/3) and Silver Myr (1/1) as blockers - they can block at most 2 creatures. Sending in Falconer and Bond-Kin forces Gramps to block both or die. Even one getting through deals 2 damage for lethal. Coach also has Heron's Grace Champion (flash, 3/3) in hand as a combat trick if needed.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose not to attack at all, leaving Gramps alive at 2 life.
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Gramps with Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin (and possibly Eldrazi Spawn). With only two blockers available, at least one 2-power creature gets through for lethal damage.

annotations.description: GLM47 Gramps is at 2 life. Gem3F has Sigarda (4/5 flying) which can attack into Gramps. Even though Katsumasa (3/3 flying) can block, Sigarda kills Katsumasa in combat and survives, removing Gramps' only flying blocker. Next turn Sigarda attacks for lethal with no flyer to block. Not attacking here gives Gramps extra time to find answers or stabilize.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack GLM47 Gramps with Sigarda, Heron's Grace. Even if Katsumasa blocks, Sigarda kills it and survives, setting up lethal next turn against a player at 2 life with no remaining flying blockers.

annotations.description: Attacking with Gwafa Hazid, Profiteer is questionable because Gwafa is much more valuable as a tap ability creature (putting bribery counters on threats to prevent them from attacking or blocking) than as a 2/2 attacker. Tapping Gwafa to attack means he can't use his ability this turn cycle. With Coach having a growing board (Abzan Falconer, Ainok Bond-Kin with outlast synergies) and Johnny having Ravenous Baloth, Gwafa's bribery ability is very relevant for controlling threats. Additionally, attacking into opponents who could easily block a 2/2 for minimal damage isn't worth losing access to Gwafa's powerful tap ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Gwafa Hazid, Profiteer as a 2/2
annotations.betterLine: Keep Gwafa untapped to use his bribery counter ability on a threatening creature like Abzan Falconer or Ravenous Baloth, neutralizing a bigger threat than 2 damage would accomplish.

annotations.description: Declined to cast Ruinous Intrusion on Howling Mine, which benefits opponents twice as much as Coach in a 3-player game. Exiling it would also put 2 +1/+1 counters on a creature, synergizing with Abzan Falconer (flying) and Ainok Bond-Kin (first strike).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Howling Mine to continue drawing cards for all players.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Ruinous Intrusion targeting Howling Mine, putting 2 +1/+1 counters on Abzan Falconer or Ainok Bond-Kin to enable flying/first strike synergies while removing asymmetric card advantage for opponents. Though mana usage this turn is a consideration, the counter synergies make this very appealing.

annotations.description: Enduring Scalelord (4/4 flyer) would provide a much stronger immediate board presence and threat, and synergizes well with the +1/+1 counter theme (Abzan Falconer gives flying to creatures with counters, and Scalelord grows whenever counters are placed on other creatures). Heronblade Elite is a smaller creature that needs time and more Humans to become impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Heronblade Elite (enters as 2/2 with Dearly Departed), a mana dork that needs future Humans to grow.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Enduring Scalelord for 6 mana (3 Plains + Forest + Sol Ring + Eldrazi Spawn), getting an immediate 4/4 flyer that synergizes with the counter strategy and provides real board pressure in a 3-player game.

annotations.description: With Sol Ring untapped providing 2 colorless mana and Dearly Departed in the graveyard, activating Sigarda's ability to create a 1/1 Human Soldier token would result in a 2/2 token (due to Dearly Departed's +1/+1 counter) that has both flying (Abzan Falconer) and first strike (Ainok Bond-Kin). This is significant free value from an activated ability at instant speed during combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to use any abilities, passing without activating Sigarda's token-creation ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Sigarda, Heron's Grace by paying 2 mana from Sol Ring and exiling a card from the graveyard to create a 1/1 Human Soldier token that enters as a 2/2 with flying and first strike.

annotations.description: Gem3F Coach appears to have not attacked when they had safe, profitable attacks available. Sigarda, Heron's Grace is a 4/5 flyer that could attack Qwen3L Johnny (40hp) with no flying blockers available. Additionally, other creatures could potentially attack. Even with Windborn Muse taxing attacks against KimiK2 Valley, attacking Johnny with flyers and ground creatures was free value.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not declare any attackers
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, attack Qwen3L Johnny with Sigarda, Heron's Grace (4/5 flying) for free damage, and potentially with other creatures like Bastion Protector since Johnny only has Ravenous Baloth and Drumhunter as blockers.

annotations.description: Attacking with Eldrazi Spawn Token (0/1) which deals 0 damage and risks losing a mana source to a chump block. The token's sacrifice-for-mana ability has more value than dealing 0 combat damage. Additionally, attacking key utility creatures like Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin into a board with Ravenous Baloth (4/4) risks losing important pieces when Coach has Cleansing Nova in hand for a future board wipe.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all creatures including the 0/1 Eldrazi Spawn Token
annotations.betterLine: Hold back the Eldrazi Spawn Token (preserve the mana source) and possibly hold back key utility creatures like Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin to preserve the +1/+1 counter synergy engine, especially with Cleansing Nova available as a reset option.

annotations.description: Drumhunter (2/2) blocking Abzan Falconer (2/3) results in Drumhunter dying without killing the Falconer. Drumhunter is a value creature that provides card draw and mana, making this an unfavorable trade.
annotations.actionTaken: Assigned Drumhunter to block Abzan Falconer, where Drumhunter dies and the Falconer survives.
annotations.betterLine: Either block Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) with Drumhunter to trade favorably (Drumhunter survives, Bond-Kin dies), or use Ravenous Baloth (4/4) to block the Falconer (killing it while surviving), or simply take 4 damage from 40 life and preserve both creatures.

annotations.description: Chose to block Abzan Falconer (2/3) with Drumhunter (2/2) instead of Bastion Protector (3/3). Blocking Bastion Protector would prevent 1 more damage (3 vs 2) and damage a more strategically important creature that grants the commander indestructible and +2/+2. In both cases Drumhunter dies and the blocked creature survives.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Abzan Falconer with Drumhunter, preventing 2 damage and losing Drumhunter
annotations.betterLine: Block Bastion Protector with Drumhunter to prevent 3 damage instead of 2 and damage the more strategically important creature

annotations.description: At 12 life with only Ravenous Baloth as a creature, Behemoth Sledge's lifelink would be very valuable for survival. War Cadence and Terra Ravager are both situational and less impactful given the current board state and low life total.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded One Dozen Eyes and Behemoth Sledge
annotations.betterLine: Discard One Dozen Eyes and War Cadence (or Terra Ravager). Behemoth Sledge's lifelink is critical at 12 life - equipping Ravenous Baloth would create a 6/6 lifelink trampler that could stabilize the game.

annotations.description: Homeward Path only produces colorless mana and its activated ability isn't relevant right now - there are no steal effects threatening Valley's creatures. With all lands tapped and spells like Rites of Flourishing (2G), Humble Defector (1R), and Reverse the Sands (6WW) in hand, colored mana production is much more important.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Homeward Path, producing only colorless mana with an irrelevant activated ability.
annotations.betterLine: Play Gruul Turf or Selesnya Sanctuary (bouncing a tapped land to replay next turn) to develop colored mana for casting Rites of Flourishing or Humble Defector. Even Terramorphic Expanse to fetch a needed basic would better support their game plan.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Valley chose to attack Gem3F Coach (47hp) instead of Qwen3L Johnny (12hp). Johnny is at critically low life and has only a Ravenous Baloth as a blocker (no Windborn Muse tax to worry about). Windborn Muse is a 2/3 flyer, and Selfless Squire is at least 1/1 (possibly larger with counters). Attacking Johnny could apply lethal pressure or force them to sacrifice their Ravenous Baloth for life gain, weakening their board. Meanwhile, attacking Coach at 47hp with a 2/3 flyer barely dents their life total. However, Coach does have the stronger board position long-term, and Valley may want to keep Johnny alive as a buffer against Coach. The reasoning is debatable but attacking the 12hp player seems more impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Gem3F Coach (47hp) with Windborn Muse
annotations.betterLine: Attack Qwen3L Johnny (12hp) to apply lethal pressure or force them to use Ravenous Baloth's sacrifice ability for survival, weakening their already thin board

annotations.description: Equipping Swiftfoot Boots to Herald of War rather than Sigarda, Heron's Grace. Sigarda provides hexproof to the player and all Human creatures, making her the highest-value protection target. If Sigarda is removed, the entire team loses hexproof protection.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Swiftfoot Boots to Herald of War for haste and hexproof
annotations.betterLine: Equip Swiftfoot Boots to Sigarda, Heron's Grace to protect the most impactful creature on board. Herald of War getting haste for one attack is less valuable than ensuring Sigarda's continued protection of the entire board.

annotations.description: At 3 life, Johnny is in a desperate situation. They chose to activate Ravenous Baloth's sacrifice ability to gain 4 life (going to 7), but this sacrifices their only creature - a 4/4 Beast that serves as both a blocker and their only board presence. With Rampaging Baloths in hand costing {4}{G}{G} and only having access to 2 green sources (2 Forests) plus Sol Ring and Selesnya Guildgate, they can't cast it this turn. However, the decision presented is between activating Ravenous Baloth (sacrificing it) versus casting Rampaging Baloths. Since they can't cast Rampaging Baloths (insufficient green mana), sacrificing the Baloth for 4 life is understandable given their critical life total. But they should consider whether keeping the 4/4 blocker alive is more valuable than 4 life. With Gem3F Coach having tapped creatures and KimiK2 Valley having a Selfless Squire (which starts as 1/1 but could be larger), the 4/4 blocker could prevent more than 4 damage. Additionally, they have lands in hand (Boros Guildgate, Boros Garrison, Mountain, Homeward Path) they should play first. The real issue is sacrificing their only meaningful creature when they could play a land first and potentially set up for Rampaging Baloths next turn while keeping the Baloth as a blocker this turn cycle.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Ravenous Baloth's sacrifice ability to gain 4 life, sacrificing their only creature.
annotations.betterLine: Play a land first (Mountain or Homeward Path for untapped mana), keep Ravenous Baloth as a blocker this turn cycle. At 3 life, having a 4/4 blocker could prevent more damage than the 4 life gained. Next turn with an additional land drop, they'd be closer to casting Rampaging Baloths and could still sacrifice Baloth if needed before damage.

annotations.description: Discarded Boros Guildgate (which produces R or W) over Homeward Path (which only produces colorless), when the hand is full of red-intensive spells like Crater Hellion (4RR), Terra Ravager (2RR), and War Cadence (2R). Homeward Path's activated ability has minimal relevance in this game state.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Boros Guildgate
annotations.betterLine: Discard Homeward Path instead, preserving colored mana sources for the red-heavy spells in hand

annotations.description: Casting Tempt with Discovery when Qwen3L Johnny is at 6 life and could potentially be finished off soon. Tempt with Discovery lets each opponent search for a land too - giving the struggling Johnny free ramp to potentially stabilize, and giving Coach (who is at 47 life and the real threat) additional lands. With Rites of Flourishing also in hand, Valley is helping opponents ramp when the board state calls for closing out the game. Additionally, Valley has Reverse the Sands in hand which becomes more powerful the wider the life total gap is - helping opponents ramp makes it harder to maintain that advantage. That said, Valley does need lands themselves (only 7 lands with expensive cards in hand), so the ramp isn't without merit.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Tempt with Discovery, giving each opponent the option to search for a free land
annotations.betterLine: Play a bounce land (Gruul Turf or Selesnya Sanctuary) to develop mana without giving opponents free resources, or play Terramorphic Expanse and hold up mana for future turns. Focus on pressuring Johnny who is at 6 life rather than enabling group ramp.

annotations.description: KimiK2 Valley cast Humble Defector (a 2/1 that gives an opponent card draw when activated) in the postcombat main phase when they had several other productive plays available. With 8 cards in hand including Rites of Flourishing (which would help ramp and draw), bounce lands (Gruul Turf, Selesnya Sanctuary), and Reverse the Sands (which could be game-winning given the life total disparity of 28 vs 6 vs 47), casting Humble Defector is low-impact. The Defector primarily benefits opponents - it gives them cards when activated and has a tiny 2/1 body. Meanwhile, Rites of Flourishing would accelerate Valley's game plan of playing multiple lands from hand and drawing extra cards, and could be cast with the available mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Humble Defector from hand in postcombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Cast Rites of Flourishing (3 mana available from untapped lands: Island, Plains, and potentially Exotic Orchard) to accelerate land drops from the stacked hand and gain card advantage, or play a bounce land like Selesnya Sanctuary to fix mana while bouncing a basic to replay next turn with Rites.

annotations.description: At 6 life with only 6 lands (5 untapped after playing Homeward Path), Johnny is in a desperate situation. Druidic Satchel costs 3 to cast and then 2 more to activate, meaning it won't generate value until next turn at the earliest. Meanwhile, Harmonize (costing 2GG) would draw 3 cards immediately, potentially finding answers or lands to stabilize. With Gem3F Coach at 47 life having creatures on board and KimiK2 Valley at 28 life with a Selfless Squire, Johnny needs to find answers fast. Druidic Satchel is a slow value engine that's terrible when you're at 6 life and need immediate impact. The Satchel's best case next turn is revealing a land (ramp) or creature (1/1 token) or gaining 2 life - none of which meaningfully stabilize at 6 life. Harmonize finding 3 cards gives much better odds of finding something impactful.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Druidic Satchel for 3 mana
annotations.betterLine: Cast Harmonize (2GG) using Sol Ring + 2 Forests + Selesnya Guildgate to draw 3 cards and find immediate answers for the critical 6-life situation. Could also consider playing Boros Garrison first (bouncing a tapped land) to have the right mana, or at minimum play the Mountain land drop before casting spells.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Johnny is at 3 life. If Mikaeus, the Lunarch is on the battlefield with +1/+1 counters, using his ability to distribute counters before combat would give creatures flying (via Abzan Falconer) and first strike (via Ainok Bond-Kin), potentially enabling a lethal flying attack against the 3-life opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to use any instant-speed abilities before combat.
annotations.betterLine: If Mikaeus has counters, use his distribute ability to put +1/+1 counters on attackers, granting them flying via Abzan Falconer, then attack Qwen3L Johnny for lethal.

annotations.description: Casting Avacyn's Pilgrim before combat is a minor sequencing error. While the Pilgrim can't attack this turn (no haste), it reveals information unnecessarily and should generally be cast post-combat. Additionally, with Qwen3L Johnny at 3 life, Coach should prioritize attacking first to potentially deal damage before committing mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Avacyn's Pilgrim pre-combat
annotations.betterLine: Move to combat first, attack with available creatures (Ainok Bond-Kin as a 2/1) to pressure Johnny at 3 life, then cast Avacyn's Pilgrim post-combat

annotations.description: With Qwen3L Johnny at 3 life, putting the +1/+1 counter on a ground creature without one (like Bastion Protector or another non-flying creature) would grant it both flying (via Abzan Falconer) and first strike (via Ainok Bond-Kin), adding evasive damage to help ensure lethal. Herald of War already has flying naturally, so the counter doesn't grant additional evasion keywords.
annotations.actionTaken: Put the +1/+1 counter on Herald of War, which already has flying.
annotations.betterLine: Put the counter on a ground creature without a +1/+1 counter (like Bastion Protector or Trostani's Summoner) to grant it flying and first strike via Falconer/Bond-Kin, maximizing evasive attackers against the 3-life opponent.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Johnny is at 3 life and Gem3F Coach has Sol Ring untapped. Could have used Sigarda's activated ability ({2}, exile a card from graveyard: create 1/1 Human Soldier token) to create an additional attacker/blocker for free value, especially relevant with a player at 3 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without using any activated abilities during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Use Sol Ring's {C}{C} to activate Sigarda, Heron's Grace's ability, exiling a card from the graveyard to create a 1/1 Human Soldier token before declaring attackers, adding pressure against the 3-life opponent.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Johnny is at 3 life with zero creatures on the battlefield to block. Gem3F Coach has numerous attackers available including Herald of War (3/3 flying), Sigarda (4/5 flying), Dawnhart Wardens (3/3), and several 2-power creatures. Any single 3+ power creature or combination of creatures totaling 3+ power attacking Johnny would be lethal with no possible blocks.
annotations.actionTaken: Failed to attack Qwen3L Johnny for lethal damage despite Johnny having no blockers at 3 life.
annotations.betterLine: Attack Qwen3L Johnny with any creature(s) totaling 3+ power (e.g., just Herald of War or Sigarda alone) to eliminate a player. The remaining attackers could still pressure KimiK2 Valley.

annotations.description: Qwen3L Johnny is at 3 life with no creatures to block. Abzan Falconer (2/3) and Ainok Bond-Kin (2/1) can attack for 4 total damage, which is lethal. Attacking KimiK2 Valley instead misses a guaranteed kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to attack KimiK2 Valley
annotations.betterLine: Attack Qwen3L Johnny with Abzan Falconer and Ainok Bond-Kin for lethal damage (4 damage vs 3 life)

annotations.description: Qwen3L Johnny is at 3 life with no creatures to block. Abzan Falconer is a 4/4 (with flying from its own ability since it has +1/+1 counters). Attacking Johnny would be lethal (4 damage to a 3-life player with no blockers). Instead, Coach attacked KimiK2 Valley who is at 28 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked KimiK2 Valley (28 life) with Abzan Falconer (4/4) and Eldrazi Spawn Token (1/1) for 5 damage
annotations.betterLine: Attack Qwen3L Johnny (3 life) with Abzan Falconer (4/4) for lethal damage, eliminating a player from the game

annotations.description: Gem3F Coach declined to activate Sigarda, Heron's Grace's ability ({2}, exile a card from graveyard: create a 1/1 Human Soldier token) despite having Sol Ring untapped to pay for it and multiple cards in the graveyard to exile. This is a free token that costs no cards from hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined all instant-speed actions during combat
annotations.betterLine: Activate Sigarda's ability using Sol Ring's {C}{C} to create a 1/1 Human Soldier token for free, gaining an extra body for blocking, attacking, or synergies with +1/+1 counter effects

annotations.description: At 3 life against a 102-life opponent, the player's reasoning incorrectly concluded they only had 1 green source when they actually had 2 Forests + Selesnya Guildgate (3 green sources). With Sol Ring providing {C}{C} and two Forests providing {G}{G}, Harmonize was castable this turn. Drawing 3 cards at 3 life is potentially game-deciding for finding answers or a path to survival.
annotations.actionTaken: Failed to recognize Harmonize was castable, likely leading to a wasted turn without casting the critical draw spell.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain as land drop, then cast Harmonize using Sol Ring ({C}{C}) + Forest ({G}) + Forest ({G}) to draw 3 cards and find answers while at critically low life.

annotations.description: At 3 HP against an opponent at 102 HP, the player incorrectly concluded they couldn't cast Harmonize ({2}{G}{G}) when they had 5 untapped lands producing GGG+CC (more than enough). They also appear to have skipped their land drop (Mountain was in hand, land_drops_used shows 0). Playing Mountain first then casting Harmonize would draw 3 desperately needed cards in a nearly hopeless position, and still leave mana for Druidic Satchel activation.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Druidic Satchel activation instead of casting Harmonize, missing both the land drop and the critical draw-3 spell.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain (land drop), then cast Harmonize using 2 Forests + Selesnya Guildgate + any colorless land for {2}{G}{G}, drawing 3 cards to find answers at critically low life. Then activate Druidic Satchel with remaining 2 mana.

annotations.description: At end of turn with 2 untapped mana available (Sol Ring is tapped, but Selesnya Guildgate, Forest, Forest, Homeward Path, and Contested Cliffs are untapped), Druidic Satchel activation costs {2} + tap. This is a pure upside mana sink at end of opponent's turn - it could reveal a creature (getting a 1/1 token chump blocker, critical at 3 life), a land (free ramp), or a noncreature/nonland spell (2 life, also critical at 3 life). There's no reason to hold mana open since it's the end step and no instants in hand. Declining a free value activation when at 3 life is a clear mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Druidic Satchel, reasoning 'no reason to' and 'save mana'.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Druidic Satchel using 2 of the available untapped lands. At 3 life, gaining 2 life, getting a chump blocker, or hitting a free land are all highly valuable outcomes with zero downside.
